$comment: Every file declaring 'use client' MUST appear here. Enforced by lint rule
brs/client-component-allowlist (implementation_plan.md §13.4 rule 5).
WHY: the Next.js 15 App Router ships a ~110 KB gzip React runtime floor
before a line of our code. The only budget we control is first-party JS,
capped at 15 KB (§4.7). That budget erodes one convenient 'use client' at
a time, so adding an island must be a deliberate, reviewable act.
Phase L permitted exactly TWO islands, listed first below.
THE MOTION SHEET ADDS FOUR MORE, and the budget argument above no
longer applies to them. That page is a pitch artefact built on client
instruction ('just need best of the best UI to show and convince the
club members'); it carries GSAP and Lenis by design, so counting its
islands against a 15 KB budget would be measuring the wrong thing.
The entries are still required, and still reviewed, for the other
reason this file exists: an island is a thing that can break with JS
disabled, and each one below has to say what happens when it does.
Before adding an entry, ask: can this be a Server Component? On an
archive site the answer is almost always yes.
THE ADMIN AREA (/admin) is a client application by necessity and the
budget argument does not apply to it: it is authenticated, it is
noindex, no visitor ever loads it, and Next code-splits it away from
every public route. It cannot work without JavaScript, and that is
stated rather than pretended otherwise — signing in and writing to a
CMS is not a no-JS activity.

allow.reason: Scroll-position observation and aria-current updates on the zone rail. Must remain a real <nav> of anchor links, keyboard traversable (§4.3).
Drag/wheel scrubbing and arrow-key navigation on the 2005-2026 Record axis. Renders as a semantic <ol> and becomes a static list under prefers-reduced-motion (§4.5).

The B-R-S opening timeline. WITHOUT JS: never renders, so the page opens directly on the Opening section with nothing missing. Skips on click or any key, removes itself entirely under prefers-reduced-motion, and carries a 4s failsafe so a stalled timeline can never leave the page locked behind an overlay.
Lenis scroll interpolation feeding ScrollTrigger. Renders null. WITHOUT JS: the browser scrolls natively, which is the correct fallback. Not installed at all under prefers-reduced-motion.

Scrub-linked un-skew of three figure plates. WITHOUT JS: the three plates are already in their final positions in the DOM and simply render as a static row — the transforms are the entrance, not the layout.

Pinned vertical-to-horizontal traverse. WITHOUT JS, and below 768px: the same track becomes a native snap-scrolling horizontal list, so the content is reachable by touch, keyboard and scrollbar with no pin at all.
Nine plates converging into a 3x3 grid. WITHOUT JS: the grid renders complete and static, because the plates are translated from their final cells rather than positioned elsewhere.

Scroll-scrubbed canvas of a 240-frame exploded-view assembly. Frames are decoded up front and the pin is not armed until they are ready. WITHOUT JS, under prefers-reduced-motion, and below 768px: renders a single static frame as a plain with full alt text and fetches none of the 9 MB sequence.
Holds the signed-in user for the whole admin area. Without JS there is no session and no admin panel; the public site is unaffected.
Admin frame: navigation, sign-out, and the redirect to /admin/login. Shows only what the signed-in role can do.
Form controls, notices and confirmations for the admin area.
Uploads a photograph through the ingest service and picks an existing one.
The sign-in form.
Overview: the approval queue and your recent posts.
Blog post list.
Write, submit and approve a blog post.
Upload and describe photographs.
Committee sections, positions and members in one screen.
Everyone on record.
The list of events, shown as the feed shows them — cover, name, kind, year, live or draft — with a search box, because nineteen of them are called some version of "Basic Workshop".
Create an event: name, cover, summary, the description, and Publish. The archive fields — category, date, venue — sit behind one disclosure so the form does not open on a wall of empty boxes.

Choosing what kind of event this is, and adding a kind that does not exist yet. Categories moved out of a Postgres enum into a table in migration 0015, so the club can file an event under something nobody thought of in 2026. Two selects rather than a tree, because the structure is only ever two levels deep. Creating is inline because the alternative — a separate screen — means abandoning a half-written write-up, which in practice means nobody adds a category and everything gets filed under whichever existing one is closest.

Uploading a photograph through @brs/ingest, so it is resized, re-encoded, EXIF-stripped and content-addressed rather than stored as the original phone file. Shared by the full picker (cover, portraits) and the file-only uploader inside the write-up editor: the two differ in how much they ask the person, and must not differ in what they do with the file.
Competition results, with the verification rule enforced in the form.
Partners and press coverage.
Create and remove accounts; assign Administrator or Member.
List/add/edit/delete for the collections with no workflow behind them (events, achievements, partners, press, people). One implementation instead of five near-identical screens.
Live client-side data sync for executive committee updates on refresh in local development and production. WITHOUT JS: Falls back to pre-rendered static committee HTML.
Interactive public photo archive gallery with search and lightbox preview. Filtered to exclude committee member portraits.
Category and year filtering on the events feed. WITHOUT JS: every event renders unfiltered in feed order — only the filters stop working, and on an archive that is the correct failure.

Enlarged view of an event's photographs, with arrow-key navigation, focus return and scroll lock. WITHOUT JS: the contact sheet renders as a plain grid at full size with descriptions; only the enlargement is lost.

The write-up editor, shared by events and posts. Tiptap over ProseMirror, replacing a contenteditable driven by the deprecated document.execCommand — which could not express a font, a colour, an alignment, an inline picture or a video. Stores the DOCUMENT TREE as JSON, never HTML: the published page is rendered from that tree at build time by lib/richtext/render.ts, which emits only tags it wrote itself, so author-supplied markup still cannot reach a reader.

The formatting bar: paragraph style (h2/h3/h4/quote), six fonts, the size scale, bold/italic/underline/strike/code, ink and highlight swatches, links, alignment, line spacing, lists, picture, video, rule, button, columns, an Insert menu for the remaining blocks, and a table group that appears only when the cursor is in a table. Every control maps to something lib/richtext/render.ts can publish.

The Tiptap pieces that have to know about this site. For a write-up: the style mark (token names, not CSS), line spacing, the inline picture (an asset id, not a URL, so it keeps its derivatives and EXIF strip) and the video (provider plus id, so no third-party markup is ever stored). For an announcement page: a button, a row of columns and the cards in it, a callout, a spacer, an accordion, a full-width band, and tables over the already-installed prosemirror-tables. Includes every in-editor node view.

Add-a-link (text to display + address), add-a-picture (multi-select from the library, or upload straight into the writing) and add-a-video (a URL, never an embed code). WITHOUT JS: no admin panel at all, as above.

Type "/" at the start of a block and get the block list — the keyboard half of the pair whose other half is the toolbar's Insert menu. Hand-rolled rather than @tiptap/suggestion: the trigger is a slash at the start of an empty block in a single-author editor, which is three fields of state, not a dependency. WITHOUT JS: no admin panel at all, as above.
Runs the same two renderers the content build runs, so Preview is the article rather than an approximation of it.

Fit / Desktop / Tablet / Phone above the writing box, narrowing it to the column an article actually gets on that screen — 1200, 706 and 342, derived from the page's own layout classes rather than from the device widths, because a 390px phone does not give an article 390px. It works because the write-up's breakpoints are container queries against .prose.rt-doc, so narrowing the box IS the phone; under media queries it would have shown a narrow box still laid out for a desktop. The choice lives in a module-level value so the Write and Preview bars agree. WITHOUT JS: no admin panel at all, as above.

A grab handle beside whichever block the pointer is over, so any block can be picked up and dropped somewhere else in the document. A ProseMirror plugin rather than a node view, because it has to serve nodes this project does not own — StarterKit's paragraph, heading, list and quote. The drop itself is delegated to ProseMirror via view.dragging, so the schema decides what may land where. WITHOUT JS: no admin panel at all, as above.
One fetch per photograph rather than one per render, so an article with twelve inline pictures does not re-request them on every keystroke.

§02 of the team dossier: one sentence pinned and revealed clause by clause. WITHOUT JS, and under prefers-reduced-motion: the clauses are rendered at full opacity by the server and the effect is what dims them, so the section is simply the finished sentence with no pin — the correct failure for a statement of purpose.

§04, the optional flagship: hairline leader lines drawn onto a photograph of the machine, each arriving with a placard. WITHOUT JS: the lines carry no dash attributes until the effect measures them, so the finished diagram renders. Below 768px the callouts are not positioned at all and become a plain register beneath the photograph, and no timeline is built.

§06, the competition record as a pinned horizontal chronology, and the climax of the page. Same derived pin length as the motion sheet's gallery. WITHOUT JS, below 768px, and under prefers-reduced-motion: the identical track becomes a native snap-scrolling list, so every campaign is reachable by touch, scrollbar and keyboard with no pin.
